source.title: Where Do Legal Factors Live in LLMs?

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies whether CATO legal-factor labels can be read from model activations and SAE features. It does not test whether neuron poles have one main job, whether neuron explanations predict activations, or whether neuron-level attribution graphs explain behavior.
record.gate_note: The reported results concern prediction of expert-defined legal-factor labels from pooled activations or selected SAE features, not semantic jobs of individual neurons or poles. The readouts are tested on held-out passages, but that does not test the explanation-predictiveness claims in V6 or V7. Rows record the internal-representation findings as a different construct.
record.test_reason: The study fits linear probes and selected-SAE-feature readouts to predict CATO legal-factor labels from mean-pooled residual activations of Qwen3-1.7B, Qwen3-8B and Gemma-2 2B. It never examines individual MLP neurons or neuron poles. It does not score neuron explanations by activation simulation, does not build attribution graphs, and does not revisit InceptionV1 examples. It cites superposition and SAE work only as background. No result bears on V1–V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The authors conclude that all 26 CATO factors are readable from full activations and that one or a few selected SAE features give strong readouts. They frame the work as a proof of concept on controlled narratives and leave causal dependence to future intervention experiments.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses linear probes and SAE-feature readouts to predict legal-factor labels from pooled passage activations. It does not apply the neuron-pole auditing, neuron explanation scoring, or attribution-graph methods described in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Readout performance varies with feature selection and sampled layer; the paper reports results at middle layers and per-factor best layers.

fits_no_version.finding: Linear probes on full residual activations reach held-out AUC 0.998–1.000 for all 26 CATO factors in all three models. One selected SAE feature gives mean AUC about 0.94–0.95 at the middle layer, and five features about 0.986–0.988. TF-IDF also scores near-perfectly, so the readouts are not separated from surface wording.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Expert-defined legal-factor labels are linearly decodable from pooled LLM activations and from a few selected SAE features, on controlled passages.

fits_no_version.finding: Some SAE features are selected for two related factors. In Qwen3-1.7B, layer 7 / feature 20148 is selected for both F16 and F25, and feature 14203 for both F20 and F24. F24 and F27 share a selected feature in Qwen3-8B and in Gemma-2 2B. The 26 factors select 24–25 distinct coordinates per model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Single SAE features can serve as readouts for semantically related legal factors. This concerns SAE features, not neurons.

record.problems: The evidence uses controlled English narratives about U.S. trade-secret factors, and the training and test passages share a controlled generation procedure. TF-IDF also performs near perfectly, so the results do not separate internal factor information from wording that expresses the factors. The models are small by current standards, and the authors note that intervention experiments are needed to test whether outputs depend on selected features.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results directly bear on the claim versions. Corpus-generation and human-audit statistics validate labels rather than test neuron interpretability.

untested.parts: All: neuron-pole job shares in Qwen3-32B.
All: neuron interpretability shares across models and scales.
All: reinterpretation of canonical polysemantic neurons.
All: causes of messy neurons and tool- or architecture-driven interpretability shares.
All: whether explanations from activating examples predict where neurons fire.
All: simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's relation 'discusses' is changed to 'cites_only': the paper only cites the superposition, monosemanticity and SAE literature as background. Rows R1–R19 are correctly unlinked (versions ["none"]). They measure SAE-feature or probe readouts of externally defined labels, not neuron poles or the predictiveness of neuron explanations. Their cannot_determine states are consistent with that. R1, R5 and R9 are random-feature reference values, and R4, R8 and R12 are full-vector comparators, both correctly marked as comparators. The Jaccard stability results for Qwen3-8B and the layer-distribution counts are not recorded as rows but bear on no version. No instructions appear in the text.

versions.untested_parts: Whether neuron poles have one or two main jobs, and the stated Qwen3-32B audit shares.
Interpretability shares across models, architectures, and scales up to trillions of parameters.
Whether classic polysemantic-neuron examples reflect coherent shared features or recursive generalization.
Whether architecture, regularization, or tools explain interpretability shares, including the stated InceptionV1 estimates.
Whether attribution graphs using a model's own neurons explain behavior without a replacement model or its reconstruction error.
Whether explanations fitted to activating examples fail to predict where individual neurons fire.
Automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.
